svg.desc: Worlds and Thread atlas. Story order progresses downward. Connections use reserved routing space. Full relationship and citation ledgers follow the chart. The HTML companion contains the complete accessible model.
svg.text: Knot topology - Winden eras linked by the cave corridor
2D · categorical world columns · Story-order ranks, not elapsed time. Equal ranks do not assert physical simultaneity.
Amber S± — Split outcomes. + and − are signs, not fates.
Blue T — Directed transfers. B body · M memory · C consciousness · S signal · ? literal/unspecified mechanism.
Emerald V / L — Numbered visits and explicit links only. Emerald centre on a cable means the route follows that connection.
Slate rail — World identity. Cutoff means chart boundary, not destruction. Crossings are bridges; only markers are joins.
Evidence / fate — [n] opens the evidence record. × dead · ● alive · ? unknown · ∅ nonexistent. Purple dotted connections are annotation references.

{"id": "canon", "kind": "canon_statement", "text": "Winden's cave connects 1920, 1953, 1986, 2019, 2053. Jonas travels between eras; Martha dies in 2019
(S2) and an alternate Martha saves Jonas (S3). The Unknown exists across eras. Charlotte is Elisabeth's daughter; Elisabeth is Charlotte's daughter - a
bootstrap pair. Adam (old Jonas) and Eva orchestrate the knot; S3 ends with the origin world deleting both knot worlds.", "title": "Dark S1-S3 (Netflix)"}
{"id": "allocation", "kind": "test_fixture", "text": "Eras are charted as lanes (preexisting). Cave trips are transfers (time_travel, body). The
Charlotte/Elisabeth bootstrap is recorded as genealogy edges + a closed cycle object per schema; render support for cycles is OPEN (E244). The
origin-world deletion is a beat, not a universe split (knot worlds preexist).", "title": "Fixture allocations"}
